prompt:
Score each onboarding change. Sub-scores:
- impact 0-3: how many users the targeted step loses and how much this could recover
- evidence 0-3: whether the funnel and the support mail both point at this problem
- confidence 0-2: how likely this kind of change works, judged from the lessons below
- cost 0-2: 2 = config only, 0 = needs new screens and a release
Also give predicted_lift: expected relative change in the target step's conversion, e.g. 0.05.

Lessons from earlier weeks:
Predictions were consistently too high across all tests, as no test produced statistically significant wins.
Split-screen redesigns for adoption persona selection significantly worsened performance.
Adding background processing desktop alert systems significantly worsened performance.
Adding new screens, photo quality hints, or wait progress indicators showed no clear effect.
Reordering sign-in steps, updating security copy, or adding setup checklists showed no clear effect.

Measured so far, by kind of change (relative change on the target step):
- adoption, hint: -4.7% over 1 test(s)
- adoption, redesign: -9.4% over 1 test(s)
- finish, layout: +3.7% over 1 test(s)
- finish, new_screen: -9.1% over 1 test(s)
- home, notification: -6.9% over 1 test(s)
- home, wait_info: +0.4% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, copy: -4.0% over 1 test(s)
- sign_in, reorder: -1.7% over 1 test(s)

Funnel:
- choose_path: 76.2%, median 8s / mean 514s
- sign_in: 72.9%, median 3s / mean 567s
- adoption: 60.9%, median 89s / mean 1017s
- home: 81.3%, median 201s / mean 2336s
- finish: 64.8%, median 395s / mean 5815s
- finishing onboarding overall: 17.8%

Return JSON {"scores": [{"index": i, "impact": n, "evidence": n, "confidence": n, "cost": n,
"predicted_lift": x, "note": short}]}

Changes:
0: [sign_in, redesign] Spotlight Sign-In Layout with Instant Sync Assurances: Redesign the sign-in screen using a spotlight layout that prominently highlights sign-in options alongside instant profile sync assurances. (why: Support receives 8 emails regarding missing or reset pets after signing back in, and sign_in conversion drops to 72.9%.)
1: [finish, redesign] Centered Welcome Layout for Final Desktop Hand-Off: Redesign the home_intro screen into a centered focal card highlighting immediate pet placement on the user's desktop. (why: Finish conversion drops to 64.8% with high dropoff (overall completion 17.8%), and users report confusion about pet desktop visibility.)
2: [home, wait_info] Desktop Visibility Tip Carousel on Waiting Screen: Add a subtle tip carousel component to the waiting screen explaining how the pet window layer functions on the desktop. (why: Home drop-off takes median 201s / mean 2336s, and support reports multiple inquiries about pet desktop visibility and controls.)
3: [choose_path, layout] Two-Column Path Choice Screen Redesign: Switch the choose_path screen to a clean two-column layout to clearly contrast standard pet selection against custom pet creation. (why: Path selection takes a mean of 514s, indicating users pause to weigh custom vs pre-made pet paths.)
4: [adoption, copy] Direct Desktop Activation Copy on Adoption Certificate: Update the adoption certificate screen text to emphasize that completion instantly launches the pet directly onto the desktop. (why: Multiple support emails mention pets failing to appear on the desktop or confusion around setup completion.)
5: [sign_in, copy] Desktop Re-Sync Sign-In Assurance Copy: Rephrase sign-in header and body copy to stress automatic companion backup and cross-reboot persistence. (why: 8 support emails complained about missing or reset pets after signing back in.)
6: [finish, hint] System Tray Controls Hint on Intro Screen: Add a persistent helper hint on the home_intro screen telling users to look for the desktop system tray icon to control their pet. (why: Support received 7 emails asking how to control, hide, or talk to the pet after completing onboarding.)

scores.note: High evidence from sign-in dropoff and emails, but screen redesigns consistently worsen conversion.
Finish step has major dropoff and user confusion, but redesigns carry a strong negative track record.
Home step has good conversion despite long duration; wait_info previously produced a slight positive (+0.4%).
Only backed by duration metric with no support emails; layout redesigns are high effort and risky.
Targets lowest-converting step (60.9%) backed by support emails; copy changes are low cost.
Strong evidence from 8 support emails, but sign_in copy changes previously yielded -4.0%.
Addresses 7 support inquiries at a high dropoff step with simple copy/hint configuration.
